comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: Fewer than 10 genuine comparables exist: the other enrichers (Urenco, Orano, General Matter, GLE/Silex) are private, state-owned or pre-revenue, and the uranium miners and SMR developers are loss-making. The discount persists because the core resells mostly Russian SWU whose US waivers end after 2027 and the Orano supply runs to 2030: a finite stream (~3 years of EBITDA at 10% is ~2.5x), with no owned capacity until 2029; the peers own long-lived operating assets with growing earnings.

thesis_break_reason: $30 is my horizon cash floor (net cash ~$576M + Westerman $116M + core run-off $60M over 25.1M shares = $29.96). Trading there would mean the market expects cash to be burned on a failed or overrun build, a distressed raise, or loss of the DOE milestones (a denied TENEX waiver plus a forced raise; a first capex disclosure far above ~$1,400/SWU-yr; HALEU appropriations cut) rather than ordinary volatility. It sits below my $36.7 fair value, which the round-1 $60 did not.

reasoning: Skeptic lane, round 2. The supervisor's findings I accept: no disclosure supports my 3.5M SWU build (the company says only 'multi-billion'; IPFM reports a first 120-machine cascade of ~6 MTU HALEU/yr and a 12 MTU target), so phase 1 is resized to the $2.4B definitive book (~1.3M SWU) plus 6 MTU HALEU, with phase 2 as an option; SBC shares removed; lock-up 11-08; HALEU-demand and DOE-appropriations risks added; thesis break moved below fair value. I keep my own, harsher view on unit cost (~$1,400/SWU-yr, 2x Orano IKE) and margin (40% cash, Urenco EBITDA 38.4%), which makes phase 1 alone NPV-negative and the whole build about zero NPV once the risked DOE milestones (+$596M at 6%) are added. Filings carry the bear case: TENEX supplies well over half of LEU deliveries through 2027 with the waiver pending and none after 2027; Q2 SWU price +3% vs cost +13%; HALEU operation contract unfunded; $1.2B converts plus a $500M equity/warrant raise and 10-Q warnings of large follow-ons; the KHNP/POSCO MOU only explores investment. Sell side keeps cutting (Needham $262 -> $206 on 2026-10-20, verified; UBS $170 in June; Jefferies Hold $169). Legs: engine DCF $30.5, EV/EBITDA 5x $33.9, market-share states $31.8, floor plus options $52.7 => fair value $36.7. Ladder: today's price beats model blends, so I centre ~$77 (mixture of lognormals around $72 and $115, sigma ~0.7 from 89% realised vol), P(>= $110) 0.33, P(>= $27) 0.93. Research limited: the Zacks expansion article was bot-blocked and Nasdaq returned 503; no October 2026 TENEX decision or Q3 date notice found.

model_inputs.structure_note: Method-fit flagged LEU (EBITDA margin 3.6% TTM; net cash 29% of market cap), so value is carried by: (1) net cash at the horizon (net_debt_horizon -576) and Westerman at cost (+116); (2) the Piketon build as an rNPV 'adjustment' in two programmes, LEU phase 1 (peak $280M, 0.75 x 0.85) and a 6 MTU HALEU cascade (peak $86M, 0.75 x 0.65), with the full post-horizon gross build spend ($1,425M nominal) as probability-weighted dev_costs; (3) the DOE $900M task-order milestones as a separate risked adjustment (+596, government payer at 6%); (4) two custom legs: market-share states (method b, $31.84) and cash floor plus options (method e, $52.69). The years model only the CORE business (SWU/uranium resale + residual Technical Solutions) with maintenance capex; FY2028 is the first year without Russian supply for US customers, so the core fades by design. Phase 1 alone is NPV-negative at ~$1,400/SWU-yr and $215/SWU (rNPV -704 incl. dev costs); with the DOE milestones and HALEU the build is about zero NPV, which is the skeptic thesis.
model_inputs.gap_note: Judgment calls for Kilian: (a) build capex is undisclosed ('multi-billion'); I use ~$1,400/SWU-yr x ~1.55M SWU-yr (1.3M LEU + 0.25M HALEU) = ~$2.2B gross for phase 1, ~2x Orano IKE's ~$676/SWU-yr (~$5B / 7.4M SWU) for a first-of-a-kind, small-scale US build. Variant at Orano's cost: rNPV dev costs fall ~$560M -> DCF leg +$22/share, fair value about +$11 (+30%): FLAG (>5%). (b) Base sizes HALEU at the disclosed first 120-machine cascade (6 MTU/yr) rather than the stated 12 MTU target, because HALEU demand rests on pre-licence reactors; 12 MTU in the base adds ~+$3/share. (c) Build success 0.75 x 0.85 = 0.64 from the US greenfield record (Urenco USA built; ACP, Eagle Rock, GLE Paducah not) lifted for DOE money, the Russian ban and the 2023-25 HALEU cascade run. (d) Net cash at the horizon (-576) and shares (25.1M) are derived, incl. a 0.5 x $400M raise; the Q3 10-Q (~early Nov) resets them. (e) DOE milestones taken pre-tax (depreciation on the cascades and NOLs shield them); taxed at 21% they would be -$5/share. (f) LEU inventories and NOLs not valued separately (core run-off $60M covers inventory sell-down). Versus consensus: StockAnalysis forward P/E 40.82 at $109.88 implies NTM EPS ~$2.69; my FY2027 core GAAP EBIT is $64M (~$2.0/share after tax before expensed pre-op build cost), >25% below, because LEU margin keeps compressing and pre-op cost is expensed; Westerman (~$160M revenue) is carried at cost, not in my revenue. Fair value = engine base horizon value; the price ladder sits above it (median ~$77) because today's price beats model blends as a 12-month forecast.

model_inputs.dcf_check: The engine DCF ($30.46) sits ~25% below the other legs because it values the core resale business fading after the 2027 ban deadline plus the build at its rNPV: LEU phase 1 -$704M (unrisked inflows $603M x 0.64 vs $1,088M risked spend), HALEU +$81M, DOE milestones +$596M, i.e. the build is about zero NPV at the 9.9% WACC. The option leg is higher because it credits the right to stop spending and phase 2; the market-share leg is close to the DCF. I keep the tested 0.40 weight.
